tasks.commit: feat(qa): orphaned-NPC detector for game project manifests
tasks.spec:
Create a deterministic orphaned-NPC detector for babylon-cinema game-project manifests. Work ONLY in this directory.

FIRST read examples/game-engine/pharmacy-help-pt-a2/project.json and examples/game-engine/coffee-order-en-a1/project.json to learn the REAL JSON shape: NPCs are defined in scenes[].entities[].components[] (a component with kind "dialogue.npc" carrying config.npcId) and referenced in oralTaskGraphs[].nodes[] that have an npcId. Match the detector to the actual shape.

Create EXACTLY these two files (touch nothing else):
1) scripts/qa/orphaned-npcs.ts exporting function findOrphanedNpcs(project: unknown): { undefinedRefs: string[]; unused: string[] } where defined = config.npcId from dialogue.npc components, referenced = npcId from oralTaskGraphs nodes, undefinedRefs = referenced minus defined (sorted unique), unused = defined minus referenced (sorted unique). Be defensive: tolerate missing arrays/fields, never throw. Add a CLI: when run as tsx scripts/qa/orphaned-npcs.ts <project.json>, parse the file, print JSON {ok, undefinedRefs, unused} (ok true when undefinedRefs empty) and process.exit(1) if any undefinedRefs.
2) test/qa/orphaned-npcs.spec.ts (vitest): import findOrphanedNpcs with a NodeNext specifier ending in .js using the CORRECT relative depth (the test sits in test/qa/, the script in scripts/qa/, so use ../../scripts/qa/orphaned-npcs.js). Load both example project.json files and assert undefinedRefs length 0 for each. Inline fixture: one NPC defined (dialogue.npc config.npcId "baker") and an oralTaskGraph node referencing npcId "ghost" not defined; assert undefinedRefs equals ["ghost"] and unused equals ["baker"].

HARD RULES: TypeScript only. NodeNext ESM import specifiers end in .js. Comments only explain WHY. No new deps. Surgical: ONLY those two files. VERIFY by running: npx vitest run test/qa/orphaned-npcs.spec.ts and ensure it passes. If genuinely blocked, STOP and report.

tasks.commit: feat(qa): dangling-portal detector for game project manifests
tasks.spec:
Create a deterministic dangling-portal detector for babylon-cinema game-project manifests. Work ONLY in this directory.

FIRST read examples/game-engine/pharmacy-help-pt-a2/project.json and examples/game-engine/coffee-order-en-a1/project.json to learn the REAL JSON shape: discover the actual scene id key (e.g. scenes[].id) and the actual portal destination field (scenes[].portals[] with a target scene id field). Match the detector to the actual shape.

Create EXACTLY these two files (touch nothing else):
1) scripts/qa/dangling-portals.ts exporting function findDanglingPortals(project: unknown): { dangling: Array<{ portalDestination: string; fromScene: string }> }. Collect all valid scene ids; for every portal whose destination is non-empty and NOT a valid scene id, record it. Be defensive, never throw. CLI: tsx scripts/qa/dangling-portals.ts <project.json> prints JSON {ok, dangling} (ok true when dangling empty) and process.exit(1) if any dangling.
2) test/qa/dangling-portals.spec.ts (vitest): import findDanglingPortals with a NodeNext specifier using the CORRECT relative depth ../../scripts/qa/dangling-portals.js (the test is in test/qa/). Load both example project.json files and assert dangling length 0 for each. Inline fixture: two scenes (ids "home", "bakery") and a portal in "home" whose destination is "void" (not a real scene). Assert dangling length 1 referencing destination "void" from scene "home".

HARD RULES: TypeScript only. NodeNext ESM import specifiers end in .js (use ../../ depth). Comments only explain WHY. No new deps. Surgical: ONLY those two files. VERIFY by running: npx vitest run test/qa/dangling-portals.spec.ts and ensure it passes. If genuinely blocked, STOP and report.
